properties.natural_language: A trace request received from an external requester must only be processed if the node's tracing configuration flag is explicitly enabled; otherwise the request must be rejected.
The transaction hash provided in a trace request must reference a valid, existing transaction; resource consumption for traced execution must be bounded to prevent denial-of-service.
The pre-execution state captured in a trace (pc, op, gas, stack, memSize) must reflect the EVM state immediately before the opcode executes and before any state changes from that opcode are applied.
All major Ethereum client implementations must produce identical trace output for the same transaction to enable differential fuzzing; trace field ordering, types, and encoding must be consistent.
The error field in a trace object must contain a properly encoded error description or hex-encoded revert reason; the encoding format must be consistent across implementations.
When an error occurs on a STOP opcode, no trace output line must be generated for that opcode; errors on all other opcodes must produce a trace line including the error field.

After transaction execution completes, the summary output must contain exactly four fields: stateRoot (post-transaction state trie root), output (return data), gasUsed (total gas consumed), and pass (success boolean).
Trace output must accurately reflect actual EVM execution; any discrepancy between trace data and real execution state constitutes a consensus-critical bug.
Precompiled contract calls must be traced at the CALL opcode level but internal precompile execution must not generate opcode-level trace output.
The gasCost field in each trace line must equal the gas consumed by that specific opcode execution, computed as gas_before - gas_after.
An approved external resource origin must satisfy all three mandatory requirements at all times: unique revision identification capability, proven availability history, and free access.
An origin must provide at least one valid revision identification method (git commit hashes, version numbers, or publication dates) before it can proceed to availability evaluation.
External resource origins must not modify historical resource revisions after publication; the revision identifier must always resolve to identical content.
After an origin is removed from the approved list due to a requirement violation, it must undergo the full re-evaluation process before being re-approved; no shortcut re-approval is permitted.
The term 'free access' for origin validation must mean no monetary cost is required; registration requirements without payment may be acceptable.
The re-evaluation frequency for approved origins must ensure that requirement violations are detected in a timely manner to prevent EIPs from referencing unavailable or paywalled content.

Before a block is accepted into the fork choice store, all blob sidecars referenced by the block's KZG commitments must be retrieved and batch-verified via verify_blob_kzg_proof_batch; the block must not be considered valid until this check passes.

Once a block has passed the data availability check and is added to the fork choice store, it retains its valid status even if blob data is subsequently pruned after MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS.

The on_block handler must verify in sequence: (1) parent block exists in store, (2) block timing is within acceptable bounds, (3) block descends from the finalized checkpoint, and (4) blob data is available. Any assertion failure must cause immediate block rejection.
After a block passes all fork choice assertions and state transition, the store must contain: the block keyed by root, the resulting beacon state, updated timeliness data, and updated checkpoints.
Extraneous or invalid blobs received from the network must not invalidate otherwise-valid blocks; only blobs matching the block's KZG commitments are considered for the data availability check.

PayloadAttributes sent to the execution engine via forkchoiceUpdated must include the parent_beacon_block_root field (EIP-4788) and all other required fields; the execution engine must construct payloads faithfully per these attributes.
Blob data must remain available on the P2P network for at least MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs after block inclusion to allow syncing nodes to validate historical blocks.

A block received from a network peer for difficulty validation must have its difficulty recomputed using the Arrow Glacier formula (with bomb offset 10,700,000) and compared against the claimed header value; any mismatch must cause block rejection.

Block data received from a network peer must be validated against the correct fork rules: blocks with number >= 13,773,000 must use Arrow Glacier difficulty calculation; blocks before that must use London rules.

After computing the fake block number by subtracting 10,700,000 from the actual block number, the difficulty bomb component must be calculated as 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2); if fake_block_number < 0, it must be treated as 0.
Arrow Glacier only modifies the difficulty bomb delay parameter; all other protocol rules (EIP-1559 base fee, gas limit, transaction processing) must remain identical to the London fork.
All Ethereum clients must compute identical difficulty values for the same block inputs under Arrow Glacier rules; any client using a different bomb offset would produce a consensus-breaking fork.
An attacker manipulating block timestamps within protocol-allowed bounds must not be able to gain a meaningful difficulty reduction advantage for selfish mining under the Arrow Glacier calculation.
An account is defined as empty if and only if nonce == 0, balance == 0, and code is empty; storage state must not be considered in the emptiness determination.
After a transaction completes execution, all addresses that were 'touched' during execution must be evaluated for emptiness; any empty account must be deleted from the state trie.
The following operations must trigger an account 'touch' for emptiness evaluation: zero-value CALL, CREATE, zero-value SELFDESTRUCT, transaction target, and miner fee recipient (coinbase).
After EIP-158 activation, zero-value CALLs and SELFDESTRUCTs to nonexistent addresses must not incur the 25,000 gas account creation cost; the gas charged must reflect only the base operation cost.

Contracts must not rely on the distinction between empty and nonexistent accounts for security logic; after EIP-158, an account can transition from empty to nonexistent without explicit deletion by the account holder.

During the transition period when legacy empty accounts exist, the cost of touching an empty account (~700 gas, or ~350 with SUICIDE refund) must not enable state churn attacks that significantly increase uncle rates.
Empty accounts must not be created faster than they can be cleared; after EIP-158 activation, the net effect must be a monotonic decrease in the count of empty accounts over time.

An inclusion list retrieved from the execution engine via get_inclusion_list() must contain structurally valid transactions; a compromised execution engine returning empty or manipulated lists undermines censorship resistance.
The inclusion list must be signed using the DOMAIN_INCLUSION_LIST_COMMITTEE domain with the validator's BLS key and broadcast before the submission deadline (~67% into the slot).

After computing the attester head via get_attester_head(store, head_root), if the head block does not satisfy inclusion list requirements, the attestation must vote for the parent block instead of the raw fork choice head.

A block proposer must collect inclusion lists from the store up to PROPOSER_INCLUSION_LIST_CUTOFF_BPS (~92% of previous slot) and include the mandated transactions in the execution payload via PayloadAttributes.

Network latency must allow honest inclusion list committee members to receive blocks and broadcast their inclusion lists within the ~67% slot window; failure to meet this timing degrades censorship resistance.

An attacker controlling a minority of inclusion list committee members must not be able to prevent honest members from broadcasting their lists; network-level eclipse attacks on committee members must be mitigated.
An eth_getBlockByHash request received from a JSON-RPC client must contain a valid block hash; invalid or malformed hashes must return a null result without error.
The JSON-RPC client request block hash parameter must be validated as a properly-formatted 32-byte hex string before block lookup is initiated.

For blocks at or after the EIP-1559 fork activation, the JSON-RPC response must include the baseFee field formatted as a hexadecimal Quantity (0x-prefixed, no leading zeros); for pre-1559 blocks, the baseFee field must be omitted entirely.
The client must have accurate knowledge of the EIP-1559 fork activation block number; incorrect fork boundary knowledge could cause baseFee field to be incorrectly included or omitted.
When a block hash is not found in local storage, the response must be a JSON-RPC result with null value; no error code must be returned for missing blocks.
The baseFee value stored in and returned from block headers must be authentic and unmodified; any tampering with stored baseFee values could lead to incorrect gas price calculations by clients.
The same baseFee inclusion rules that apply to eth_getBlockByHash must also apply to eth_getBlockByNumber to ensure consistent API behavior across query methods.

The valid_jump_destinations set must be computed from bytecode analysis before execution begins and must remain immutable throughout contract execution; no runtime modification of this set is permitted.
JUMPDEST scanning must correctly skip over PUSH instruction data bytes to avoid falsely marking data bytes containing 0x5b as valid jump destinations.
Contract bytecode loaded for execution must have been deployed by an external contract deployer; the JUMPDEST scan must operate on the exact deployed bytecode without modification.
After JUMP execution with a valid destination, the program counter must be set to exactly the value popped from the stack (Uint(jump_dest)); GAS_MID (8 gas) must have been charged.

After JUMPI with condition != 0, the destination must be validated against valid_jump_destinations and PC set to the destination; with condition == 0, PC must be incremented by 1 without jump validation. GAS_HIGH (10 gas) must be charged in both cases.
When a JUMP or JUMPI targets an address not in valid_jump_destinations, an InvalidJumpDestError must be raised, execution must halt, and all remaining gas must be consumed.
After STOP opcode execution, evm.running must be set to False and program counter incremented by 1; execution must halt normally without error.
The GAS opcode must push the remaining gas value AFTER charging GAS_BASE (2 gas), showing the gas available at that point in execution.

Attackers must not be able to create valid jump destinations at arbitrary bytecode addresses through data manipulation in PUSH instructions; the scan must only recognize 0x5b bytes that are actual opcode positions.

A Type 1 transaction received from a submitter must have its access list validated for correct structure: each entry must contain a 20-byte address and a list of 32-byte storage keys; malformed entries must cause transaction rejection.

Transaction bytes received from a network peer must be validated in order: (1) type byte == 0x01, (2) valid RLP decoding, (3) exactly 11 fields, (4) correct chain ID, (5) access list structure with 20-byte addresses and 32-byte keys.

The transaction signature must be verified over keccak256(0x01 || rlp([chainId, nonce, gasPrice, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList])); the signature hash includes the access list to prevent post-signing modification.

After intrinsic gas calculation, the total must equal base_intrinsic (21000 + calldata) + (num_addresses * 2400) + (num_storage_keys * 1900); duplicate entries must be charged at full cost with no benefit.

After access list pre-warming, all listed addresses must be in accessed_addresses and all listed (address, key) tuples must be in accessed_storage_keys; subsequent SLOAD on pre-warmed keys costs 100 gas instead of 2100.
The accessed_addresses set must always contain at minimum: the transaction sender, the transaction recipient (to), and all precompile addresses, regardless of whether they appear in the access list.
Duplicate entries in an access list must be charged gas but produce no additional warming benefit; the set-based data structure ensures idempotent insertion.
Access list size is bounded only by block gas limit; very large access lists must consume proportional gas in intrinsic cost, preventing underpriced DoS through oversized lists.

Each access list address entry must have its address length validated as exactly 20 bytes and each storage key validated as exactly 32 bytes; any length mismatch must cause immediate validation failure.

A gossip message received from a peer on the beacon_block topic must have its KZG commitment count validated against MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA before acceptance; messages exceeding this limit must be REJECTED and the peer's score penalized.

A SingleAttestation received on a beacon_attestation subnet must have attestation.data.index == 0 and the attester must be verified as a member of the committee for the given slot; invalid attestations must be REJECTED.
A blob sidecar received on a blob_sidecar subnet must have its blob index and KZG commitments validated against MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA; excess blobs must be REJECTED.
An aggregate and proof message on beacon_aggregate_and_proof topic must have committee_bits with exactly 1 bit set and aggregate data index equal to 0; violations must be REJECTED.
BlobSidecarsByRange and BlobSidecarsByRoot req/resp requests must be bounded to MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA; requests exceeding this limit must return an error response.

Peers must correctly implement fork version negotiation and must not send Deneb-format messages after the Electra fork epoch; receiving nodes must strictly validate fork version to prevent consensus divergence.

The BLOB_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT_ELECTRA of 9 subnets must provide sufficient distribution capacity for the increased blob count; subnet congestion must not cause blob propagation delays that affect data availability.
Attestation subnet validation must ensure committee membership checks are fast enough to prevent DoS through flooding of valid-looking SingleAttestation messages.
BeaconBlocksByRange responses must return fork-appropriate SignedBeaconBlock types: electra.SignedBeaconBlock for Electra-era slots, and the correct prior fork types for earlier slots.
A SingleAttestation that passes all validation (data.index == 0, valid committee membership) must be accepted and propagated to other peers on the subnet.
MAX_REQUEST_BLOB_SIDECARS_ELECTRA must equal MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB * MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA; MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB is a fixed constant from Deneb and is not modified by Electra.

When responding to BlobSidecarsByRange, the responder must return all available sidecars for the first blob-carrying block in the range or none; partial sidecar sets for a block must be treated as unavailable.
